items.question: What range of flow speeds did the BASS-II wind tunnel cover?
items.answer:
The BASS-II poster gives different figures for the airflow speed:
- Main variables list: 0 to 55 cm/s [R091]
- Hardware description: the wind tunnel could impose airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s [R090]

items.question: Which tests sit nearest the Moon-base atmosphere?
items.answer:
The closest match is the FM2 plan to burn acrylic rods on the Moon in Normoxic Space Exploration Atmospheres at 8.2 psia and 34% oxygen; these burns are still planned [R073] [R075].
Nearest tests with results (reduced pressure, raised oxygen):
- Saffire VI-2, SIBAL cloth: 54.1 kPa, 31.0 mol % oxygen [R029]
- Saffire VI-3, two-sided PMMA: 54.6 kPa, 30.3 mol % oxygen [R030]
- Saffire VI-4, one-sided PMMA: 55.2 kPa, 28.8 mol % oxygen [R031]

items.question: What is the spread rate of Nomex at Mars gravity in 34% oxygen?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows have no Nomex tests and no spread rate at Mars gravity in 34% oxygen.
Nearest tests:
- Kimwipes tissue on the NASA KC-135 aircraft: downward spread rate peaks near 0.38 g, near the Martian gravity [R093]
- FM2 planned PMMA rod burn on the Moon at 8.2 psia and 34% oxygen, no result yet [R073]
- SIBAL fabric on LUCI in simulated lunar gravity: flame base spread rate 0.92 mm/s [R001]

items.question: What was the flame tip spread rate of the SIBAL fabric in lunar gravity on LUCI?
items.answer:
The SIBAL fabric flame tip spread rate in simulated lunar gravity on LUCI was 1.1 mm/s [R002].
- For comparison, the 1-g ground burn gave 2.8 mm/s [R004].

items.question: Which materials have been burned in lunar gravity, and on which platforms?
items.answer:
- SIBAL fabric (cotton/fiberglass blend): burned in air, only downward, in lunar gravity on a lunar-gravity centrifuge and in parabolic flight [R076]
- SIBAL fabric and a PMMA (acrylic) rod: burned together in simulated lunar gravity on the spinning Blue Origin New Shepard capsule (LUCI) [R026]
- PMMA (acrylic) rods: still planned for FM2 on a lunar lander [R073] [R075]

items.question: What flame spread rate has been measured in the spacesuit atmosphere of 100% oxygen at 4.3 psia?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows have no flame spread rate measured in 100% oxygen at 4.3 psia.
Nearest tests:
- Kimwipes tissue on the NASA KC-135 aircraft at 27.6 kPa (4.0 psia) in air, partial gravity [R093]
- FM2 planned PMMA rod burn on the Moon at 8.2 psia and 34% oxygen, no result yet [R073]
- SIBAL fabric on LUCI in air, simulated lunar gravity: flame base spread rate 0.92 mm/s [R001]

items.question: What peak heat release did the SIBAL sample reach in Saffire VI-2?
items.answer: The SIBAL cloth sample in Saffire VI-2 reached a peak heat release of 3217 W, by oxygen consumption calorimetry [R032].

items.question: How did LUCI's lunar-gravity flame spread rates compare with its 1 g burns?
items.answer:
Lunar-gravity spread rates were lower than the 1 g rates in each matched pair:
- SIBAL flame base: 0.92 mm/s in lunar gravity [R001] vs 1.5 mm/s in 1 g [R003]
- SIBAL flame tip: 1.1 mm/s in lunar gravity [R002] vs 2.8 mm/s in 1 g [R004]
- PMMA rod flame tip: 0.15 cm/s in lunar gravity [R007] vs 0.40 cm/s in 1 g [R008]

items.question: What flame spread rate did FM2 measure for the acrylic rod burned on the Moon?
items.answer:
No evidence: The FM2 acrylic rod burns on the Moon are planned and have no result yet [R073] [R075].
Nearest tests:
- LUCI PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: flame tip spread rate 0.15 cm/s [R007]
- LUCI PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: peak instantaneous flame base spread rate 0.6 mm/s (approximate) [R022]
- BASS-II PMMA rods in microgravity on the ISS: 54 unique flame spread rates obtained [R086]

items.question: At what oxygen level did the 1/4 inch PMMA rod blow off in normal gravity in the BASS-II work?
items.answer:
In normal gravity (1 g), the 1/4 inch PMMA rod blew off at 16% oxygen [R078].
- For comparison, BASS-II on the ISS obtained steady spreading on the same rod size at 13.6% oxygen [R079].

items.question: Which Saffire VI sample produced the largest CO increase, and how do the three samples compare?
items.answer:
Saffire VI-4 (one-sided PMMA) produced the largest CO increase at the far-field inlet, 320 ppm [R052].
- VI-4, one-sided PMMA: 320 ppm [R052]
- VI-3, two-sided PMMA: 308 ppm [R051]
- VI-2, SIBAL cloth: 120 ppm [R050]
The PMMA samples were close to each other and well above the SIBAL sample.

items.question: What was the heat release rate of the PMMA rod on the LUCI flight?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows give no heat release rate for the PMMA rod on the LUCI flight.
Nearest tests:
- LUCI PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: flame tip spread rate 0.15 cm/s [R007]
- LUCI PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: peak instantaneous flame base spread rate 0.6 mm/s (approximate) [R022]
- LUCI PMMA rod in simulated lunar gravity: lowest chamber oxygen 14.3% during the burn [R013]

items.question: What is the lowest oxygen level at which BASS-II obtained steady flame spreading in microgravity?
items.answer:
BASS-II obtained steady spreading at 13.6% oxygen, on a 1/4 inch PMMA rod in concurrent (stagnation point) flow on the ISS [R079].
- For comparison, the 1 g blowoff for the same rod size was at 16% oxygen [R078].

items.question: Compare the burn durations of the samples in Saffire IV, V and VI.
items.answer:
- IV-1, SIBAL cloth: 130 s [R027]
- V-2, cotton jersey: 200 s [R028]
- VI-2, SIBAL cloth: 112 s [R029]
- VI-3, two-sided PMMA: 780 s [R030]
- VI-4, one-sided PMMA: 1200 s [R031]
The PMMA samples burned much longer than the fabric samples. Other samples are described only qualitatively: IV-2 showed delayed extinguishment [R071], and V-3 and V-4 extinguished immediately when the fan was turned off [R069] [R070].

items.question: How fast does a flame spread over Kevlar in microgravity?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows contain no Kevlar tests.
Nearest tests:
- BASS-II PMMA rods in microgravity on the ISS: 54 unique flame spread rates obtained [R086]
- Saffire I-1 SIBAL fabric in orbit: maximum flame size 6.2 cm [R057]
- LUCI SIBAL fabric in simulated lunar gravity: flame tip spread rate 1.1 mm/s [R002]

items.question: How long did the one-sided PMMA sample burn in Saffire VI-4?
items.answer: The one-sided PMMA sample in Saffire VI-4 burned for 1200 s [R031].

items.question: How did the test conditions of Saffire IV-1 and Saffire VI-2 differ?
items.answer:
Both tests burned 50 cm long SIBAL cloth in concurrent flow at 20 cm/s [R027] [R029]. They differed in pressure and oxygen:
- Pressure: 100.0 kPa in IV-1 [R027] vs 54.1 kPa in VI-2 [R029]
- Oxygen: 22.0 mol % in IV-1 [R027] vs 31.0 mol % in VI-2 [R029]

items.question: What peak heat release did Saffire VI-1 reach?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows have no peak heat release for Saffire VI-1.
Nearest tests:
- Saffire VI-2, SIBAL cloth: peak heat release 3217 W [R032]
- Saffire VI-3, two-sided PMMA: peak heat release 3080 W [R033]
- Saffire VI-4, one-sided PMMA: peak heat release 1507 W [R034]

items.question: What rotation rate and radius did LUCI use to simulate lunar gravity?
items.answer: LUCI held a steady vehicle rotation of 11 RPM [R024], with an effective radius of rotation of 1.22 m at the experiment location [R025].

items.question: Which Saffire tests ran at reduced pressure with enriched oxygen?
items.answer:
These Saffire tests ran at reduced pressure with raised oxygen:
- V-2, cotton jersey: 70.7 kPa, 26.2 mol % oxygen [R068]
- V-3, one-sided PMMA: 71.3 kPa, 25.4 mol % oxygen [R069]
- V-4, structured PMMA: 72.6 kPa, 25.7 mol % oxygen [R070]
- VI-2, SIBAL cloth: 54.1 kPa, 31.0 mol % oxygen [R032]
- VI-3, two-sided PMMA: 54.6 kPa, 30.3 mol % oxygen [R053]
- VI-4, one-sided PMMA: 55.2 kPa, 28.8 mol % oxygen [R034]
The Saffire VI tests had the lowest pressure and highest oxygen in these rows.

items.question: What was the upward flame spread rate of PMMA at Mars gravity?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows have no PMMA flame spread rate at Mars gravity.
Nearest tests:
- LUCI PMMA rod burning upward in simulated lunar gravity: flame tip spread rate 0.15 cm/s [R007]
- LUCI PMMA rod in a 1 g ground burn: flame tip spread rate 0.40 cm/s [R008]
- LUCI PMMA rod burning upward in simulated lunar gravity: peak instantaneous flame base spread rate 0.6 mm/s (approximate) [R022]

items.question: What was the steady-state flame size of the cotton jersey sample in Saffire V-2?
items.answer:
The cotton jersey sample in Saffire V-2 had a steady-state flame size of 10.0 cm [R066].
- Its maximum flame size was 14.0 cm [R067].

items.question: How many BASS-II test points were obtained with PMMA sheets, and in which thickness ranges?
items.answer:
The rows report the PMMA sheet test points as separate sets:
- Bhattacharjee panel: 22 test points, sheets 0.1 to 0.4 mm thick [R084]
- Miller panel: 20 test points, sheets 1 to 5 mm thick [R085]

items.question: What was the burn duration of the Saffire IV-1 SIBAL sample at 34% oxygen?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows have no Saffire IV-1 burn at 34% oxygen; IV-1 ran at 22.0 mol % oxygen [R027].
Nearest tests:
- Saffire IV-1, SIBAL cloth at 100.0 kPa and 22.0 mol % oxygen: burn duration 130 s [R027]
- Saffire VI-2, SIBAL cloth at 54.1 kPa and 31.0 mol % oxygen: burn duration 112 s [R029]

items.question: What happened to the sample in Saffire V-3 when the fan was turned off?
items.answer:
The one-sided PMMA sample in Saffire V-3 extinguished immediately when the fan was turned off [R069].
- Before that, the flow was reduced from 20 cm/s to 5 cm/s and held 300 s [R069].
- The structured PMMA sample in Saffire V-4 also extinguished immediately when the fan was turned off [R070].

items.question: At which gravity levels and pressures were thin cellulose (Kimwipes) samples burned on the KC-135 aircraft?
items.answer:
- Sacksteder et al.: partial gravity of 0.1, 0.16 and 0.38 g at 27.6 kPa (4.0 psia), in air [R093] [R092]
- Feier et al.: 0.1, 0.16 and 0.38 G at 0.2-0.4 atm, in 21% O2 with balance N2 [R098]

items.question: What is the limiting oxygen concentration for SIBAL fabric in lunar gravity at 8.2 psia?
items.answer:
No evidence: The rows give no limiting oxygen concentration for SIBAL fabric in lunar gravity at 8.2 psia.
Nearest tests:
- LUCI SIBAL fabric in simulated lunar gravity: chamber oxygen fell to about 18% during the burn [R016]
- FM2 planned SIBAL fabric burns on the Moon at 14.7 psia in 21% (air), no result yet [R072] [R074]
- SIBAL fabric in lunar gravity via centrifuge and parabolic flight: burns only downward in air [R076]

items.question: Near which gravity level did the downward flame spread rate over Kimwipes peak in the KC-135 tests?
items.answer: The downward flame spread rate over Kimwipes peaked near 0.38 g, near the Martian gravity, in the KC-135 tests at 27.6 kPa (4.0 psia) in air [R093].

items.question: How did SIBAL fabric behave in lunar gravity compared with Earth gravity in the FM2 team's tests?
items.answer:
- Lunar gravity (centrifuge and parabolic flight): SIBAL fabric burned in air, but only downward [R076]
- Earth gravity: burning downward, it extinguished immediately after ignition [R077]
- The FM2 burns of SIBAL on a lunar lander are still planned [R072] [R074]
